title: add stress-probe adversarial smoke-suite + CI decider for prompt-set regression detection
author: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a new "stress-probe" smoke suite and a CI decider that runs adversarial augmentations over prompt-sets to surface regressions earlier. Motivation: standard smoke checks surface obvious breakages but miss brittle prompt cases exposed under paraphrase/adversarial perturbations. This PR adds: 1) stress-probe suite that synthesizes adversarial paraphrases, token swaps, and suffix-injection probes; 2) multi-signal gating function that combines semantic-similarity (SBERT cosine), hallucination-rate (QA-based overlap), answer-length drift, and tail latency percentiles into a single fail/pass score; 3) a CI decider hook that triggers the smoke suite only when prompt-set files or canonical examples change and uses a dynamic threshold anchored to historical percentiles; 4) cached artifact support so CI can reuse generated paraphrases for repeat runs; 5) an emergency rollback script and suggested canary rollout policy to automate mitigation when the gate trips in production. Performance/cost tradeoffs are called out in docs and the CI job is tuned to run lightweight by default (10 adversarial samples per prompt, 2 workers) and escalates locally for manual investigation. See tests and metrics in this PR for expected pass/fail behavior and the rationale for the composite scoring formula.

review_comments: Arjun Patel (review): Overall looks solid. Please reduce default sample size in CI to keep runtime < 6m and add explicit opt-out for clusters with no GPU.
Maya Chen (author): Updated default sample size to 10 and added --no-gpu flag in CI decider; added cache TTL so generated paraphrases are reused across reruns.
Sofia Martínez (review): Can you add clarity on how the composite score weights are derived and where historical baselines are stored?
Maya Chen (author): Added doc section pointing to eval-harness historical_metrics bucket and included the weight derivation script used during calibration.
Liam O'Connor (review): Tests look good. One nit: move the SBERT model loading to module-level lazy initializer to avoid repeated downloads in CI.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed lazy loading and added a small integration test to assert cache hits.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI run: stress-probe smoke job failed on hallucination-rate threshold (flaky paraphrase seed) -> reduced randomness and added deterministic replay artifact -> rerun passed. All other checks (unit, lint, types) passed. Final CI status: pass.
